sheep.builders: Eliashib the high priest, with the priests of his house. The first one standing, and the only one the record calls sanctified.

fish.builders: The family of Hassenaah. Beams, doors, bolts and bars, all on their account.

old.builders: Two men, Joiada and Meshullam, each remembered by his father's name.

valley.builders: Hanun and the people of Zanoah. Beyond the gate, a long stretch of wall, measured in cubits, up to the next one.

dung.builders: Malchijah, who ruled a district and still took the gate with the humblest name.

fountain.builders: Shallun, ruler of Mizpah. He roofed the gate, then followed the wall of the pool down to the stairs from David's city.

water.builders: The temple servants who lived on the hill of Ophel, working across from it, on the sunrise side.

horse.builders: The priests, each on the piece of wall in front of his own house.

east.builders: Shemaiah, the keeper of this gate, mended the stretch beside Zadok, who repaired the wall in front of his home.

inspection.builders: Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, up to the room above the corner. The merchants and the temple servants kept house nearby.
